meta.artefact: The controller mapping registry — every tactic->verb mapping that has been tried, what it produced, and which experiment consumed it
meta.why: The controller is the application layer the experiments vary (supervisor ruling S4). The mapping is an input parameter, not a recovered truth: there is no correct mapping to discover, every version is a choice, and this registry exists so that choices are comparable rather than overwritten. A version is selected by name at the experiment seam; the controller layer reads whatever it is given and carries no experiment's mapping of its own.

schema.tactic: ATT&CK tactic key; must match the aggregate net's tactic-places exactly
schema.sim_phase: the dispatched MTDSim verb, or empty for a dwell-only tactic
schema.disposition: 'mapped' (sim_phase names a verb) or 'dwell-only' (sim_phase empty; the tactic consumes time and dispatches nothing)
schema.ckc_phase: version-1 provenance only — the Cyber Kill Chain phase the row was composed through; empty where a version does not use CKC mediation
schema.reason: why this row holds its value; required, and the thing a reviewer reads

meta.invariant: Every tactic states mapped-to-verb or dwell-only. An empty sim_phase without a 'dwell-only' disposition is an error at load: silence stays illegal, declared absence is legal.

default_rationale: The default is the experiment-1 value, so an unqualified load reproduces what has always run. It is deliberately NOT the newest version: promoting a version to default would re-bake an experiment's choice into the pipeline, which is the coupling this registry exists to remove. Experiments select their version explicitly.

versions.name: v1_ckc_total
versions.coverage: total — all 15 tactics onto exactly one of 6 verbs
versions.construction: transitive through the Cyber Kill Chain: each verb owns one CKC phase by Brown's Fig-3 flow position, each tactic takes the verb of its own or the nearest covered phase
versions.rationale: complete coverage guaranteed by construction, chosen to get the end-to-end loop running rather than to model per-tactic behaviour
versions.produced: ASR 0.00 across all 100 movement runs, in two profile-determined failure modes: friction (up to 95% of actions blocked) and churn (hundreds of successful actions on ~2 hosts). Much of both traces to this mapping's coarseness — seven tactics on the neighbour-reveal, initial-access on a port scan.
versions.immutability_note: Frozen so experiment 1 stays reproducible. This file is a re-expression of data/ogasp/controller.csv in the registry schema; tests/l3_simulation/test_controller.py pins the two equal row-for-row, so neither can drift.

versions.name: v2_partial
versions.construction: no mediating layer: each tactic decided on its merits against what the verb actually does and requires (attacker_phase_catalogue.md), with the reason recorded per row
versions.rationale: S4 relaxes the total-coverage requirement, so a tactic with no defensible verb becomes dwell-only rather than firing a placeholder. Fixes the two rows experiment 1 most exposed: initial-access now dispatches the exploit rather than a port scan, and the objective band dispatches nothing rather than all firing the neighbour-reveal. Pairs command-and-control's neighbour-reveal with lateral-movement's host-enumeration so the substrate's native spread pair can occur.
versions.immutability_note: Becomes immutable once an experiment consumes it; until then it is still under review.
